4.findings: README describes a pure in-memory Python HTTP/2 stack, distinct from network and concurrency layers.
4.limitations: README only; current revision is not the authors modified h2 worker or a full source-code review.

6.findings: Architecture and introductory specification describe distributed end-to-end worker tests for semi-active components, with two illustrative use cases.
6.limitations: Partial review of introduction/architecture motivation; all implementation and use-case results not independently validated.

9.findings: TCP noncompliance in middleboxes can enable reflected amplification; the study uses packet-sequence exploration and Internet measurements.
9.limitations: Abstract/introduction reviewed; TCP amplification findings do not establish exploitability of the HTTP/2 cases here.

10.findings: MUST is mandatory; SHOULD permits justified exceptions; MAY defines an optional behavior. Imperatives should be reserved for interoperability or harm prevention.
10.limitations: Normative terminology alone does not map every HTTP/2 test to a correct oracle.

12.findings: Ambiguous host fields can be interpreted inconsistently across sequential HTTP processors, enabling cache poisoning or policy bypass.
12.limitations: Abstract/introduction reviewed; specific exploits, tables and target versions not re-executed.

14.findings: Project README describes a reverse proxy that handles TLS and non-TLS browser traffic and supports multi-domain mirroring.
14.limitations: Partial README review; no deployment, attack execution or binary/source audit; current revision differs from cited date.

17.findings: Survey distinguishes differentiation detection methods by network measurement, generated traffic, metrics and statistical assumptions. Congestion and load balancing can confound end-to-end inference.
17.limitations: Author manuscript abstract/introduction reviewed; 30-page survey not completely reviewed; no secondary bibliographies retrieved.

18.findings: 2017 whitepaper introduces web cache deception through disagreement between cache classification and application routing.
18.limitations: Title/introductory material reviewed; all attack demonstrations and mitigations not reviewed or tested.

19.findings: Current README describes a standalone Go reverse proxy used to mirror authenticated sessions.
19.limitations: Partial README review; cited 2024 revision not retrieved; no code audit or phishing execution.

21.findings: Watchfire whitepaper attributes request smuggling to HTTP message-boundary disagreement and discusses cache poisoning, firewall evasion and request hijacking.
21.limitations: Front matter and selected introductory material reviewed. Paper citation lists Heled alone but full text lists Linhart, Klein, Heled and Orrin. Text extraction has doubled glyphs/font warnings; no exploit validation.

22.findings: TCP-extension measurements show that middleboxes can rewrite initial sequence numbers and enforce contiguous sequence behavior; extension deployment is constrained.
22.limitations: Abstract/introduction reviewed; matching TCP sequence numbers does not exclude every intermediary. Original paths not re-measured.

23.findings: h2spec README targets RFC7540/RFC7541, expects a working 200 response with body, and exposes timeout and strict-test settings.
23.limitations: README partially reviewed; not an exhaustive RFC9113 suite and not executed in this campaign.

24.findings: Gudifu combines coverage-guided differential fuzzing with full-request discrepancy search for HTTP processors.
24.limitations: Abstract/introduction reviewed; full evaluation tables and vulnerabilities not independently validated; open-source constraints differ from cloud proxies.

25.findings: FRAMESHIFTER explores HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1 conversion anomalies across reverse proxies/CDNs using grammar-based frame manipulation.
25.limitations: Abstract/introduction reviewed; conversion anomalies require endpoint semantics beyond a generic rejection score. Exploits not reproduced.

26.findings: T-Reqs uses grammar-based differential fuzzing and explicit proxy-origin combinations to identify request parsing discrepancies.
26.limitations: Abstract/introduction reviewed; HTTP/1 parsing and exploit tests are not equivalent to this fixed HTTP/2 compliance suite.

27.findings: HTTP Garden examines origin interpretation as well as gateway transformation and uses coverage-guided fuzzing; it separates reported parsing bugs from exploitable findings.
27.limitations: Abstract/introduction reviewed; retrieved arXiv manuscript rather than a verified camera-ready version. Original corpus not re-executed.

28.findings: HTTP desynchronization depends on disagreement over message boundaries within pooled front-end/back-end connections; case studies demonstrate consequences.
28.limitations: Abstract/core-concepts sections reviewed; all case studies not reviewed. Live article updated September2025 rather than cited2024 snapshot; no exploit replication.

29.findings: HTTP/2 downgrade and implementation inconsistencies create desynchronization and request-tunnelling opportunities in specific deployment chains.
29.limitations: Introductory sections reviewed; all payload examples and cases not reviewed. Live updated article is not the original2021 snapshot.

31.findings: Cloudflare article discusses HPACK as an HTTP/2 compression feature; retrieved page identity checked.
31.limitations: Partial title/page review only; large navigation extraction obscures content. No performance or security claim adopted from this source.

32.findings: PRO-COW conducts repeated HTTP/1.1 compliance measurements over16months; version banners alone are insufficient evidence of compliance.
32.limitations: Abstract/introduction and concluding excerpts reviewed; severe extraction encoding artifacts. Full tables/figures not visually reviewed.

33.findings: Web cache deception study evaluates high-profile websites and leakage through proxy caching; marker-based detection targets a particular observable behavior.
33.limitations: Abstract/introduction reviewed; selective website sample and application/cache configurations differ from this HTTP/2 campaign.

34.findings: Follow-up web cache deception work explains limitations of marker injection/reflection and explores additional path-confusion methods.
34.limitations: Abstract and appendix excerpts reviewed; all measurements and tables not reviewed or reproduced.

35.findings: Project landing page describes interception, modification and replay features and current HTTP protocol support.
35.limitations: Landing-page introductory feature review; current v12.2 page does not describe tested v11.1.0 exactly, and does not prove compliance.

41.findings: Conformance study extracts106falsifiable rules and tests nine local servers and9990live hosts; explicit error behavior and conformance testing are recommended.
41.limitations: Author manuscript abstract/introduction reviewed, with DOI/ISBN placeholder in front matter; response conformance and web-scale sampling differ from middlebox frame tests.

42.findings: End-to-end argument places application correctness at endpoints; lower-layer functions may offer performance enhancements but cannot generally supply full application assurance.
42.limitations: Introductory and concluding argument reviewed; not a prohibition on every intermediary or empirical proof of Internet path transparency.

43.findings: HDiff combines specification extraction and differential testing to investigate semantic gaps among HTTP implementations.
43.limitations: Author manuscript abstract/introduction reviewed; generated test coverage and all vulnerability findings not independently validated.

44.findings: Censored Planet combines several remote-measurement techniques and longitudinal baselines; observations depend on protocol, vantage and inference method.
44.limitations: Abstract and appendix excerpts reviewed; event/time-series methods not independently reproduced and cannot automatically diagnose an isolated HTTP/2 timeout.

45.findings: Sections4.1/4.2 specify9octet headers,24-bit payload lengths and frame bounds. Section5.4 permits stream errors to escalate to connection errors. These constrain framing and scope checks.
45.limitations: Relevant framing/error sections reviewed; complete105-page standard and all errata not exhaustively reviewed. Generic rejection is not a complete conformance oracle.

46.findings: README describes an almost-transparent reverse proxy based on dynamic origin interaction rather than static phishing pages.
46.limitations: README reviewed, not implementation/deployment. No phishing execution or credentials collected.

47.findings: Survey discusses privacy and execution-assurance risks when middlebox processing is outsourced to an untrusted provider.
47.limitations: Abstract/introduction reviewed. Cited year2017 conflicts with downloaded issue labelled January/February2018; preserve cited and retrieved versions separately.

48.findings: 2001 position paper separates protocol compliance, compatibility and vendor-specific tests. Its256-case prototype has aborted cases and warns that many failures arise from compatibility or tool bugs.
48.limitations: Position paper and prototype counts are not a modern HTTP/2 evaluation or proof of all implementations' compliance.
